yclept.sense: adj: Called (by a certain name), named.

firstUse.quote: And as I am a Gentleman, betooke my ſelfe to walke: the time When? about the ſixt houre, […] Now for the ground Which? which I meane I walkt vpon, it is ycliped Thy Park.
firstUse.source: c. 1595–1596 (date written), W. Shakespere [i.e., William Shakespeare], A Pleasant Conceited Comedie Called, Loues Labors Lost. […] (First Quarto), London: […]

yclothed.hook: Wiktionary gives no earlier form for this sense.

ychosen.sense: verb: Archaic or obsolete form of chosen.

firstUse.quote: Ye cannot lay one finger upon us to our despite," replied the former, "if my Master permit not; for the race is neither to the swift nor the battle to the strong; for God hath ychosen ye foolish thing
